records.source: מִזְמ֗וֹר לְאָ֫סָ֥ףאֵ֤ל׀אֱֽלֹהִ֡ים יְֽהוָ֗ה דִּבֶּ֥ר וַיִּקְרָא־אָ֑רֶץ מִמִּזְרַח־שֶׁ֝֗מֶשׁ עַד־מְבֹאֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: A psalm of Asaph. [The] Mighty One, God, YHWH, has spoken and summoned [the] earth from [the] rising of [the] sun to its setting.
pieces: A psalm of Asaph. The Mighty One, God, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, has spoken; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has called to the whole earth, from the sunrise to the sunset.

L.1: A psalm of Asaph. [The] Mighty One, God, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, has spoken and summoned [the] earth from the rising of [the] sun to its setting.

R.1: A song of Asaph. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the mighty God, has spoken. He calls everyone on earth, from the far east to the far west.

decisions.choice: The title shares verse 1
decisions.reason: This psalm's title is short and the Hebrew counts it together with the first line as verse 1, so here the verse numbers are the same as in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: Asaph: a leader of the temple singers
decisions.reason: Asaph was a Levite whom David appointed to lead the singing before the ark (1 Chronicles 16:5-7); his family carried on the work. Psalms 50 and 73-83 bear his name.

decisions.choice: the Mighty One, God, YHWH: three names
decisions.reason: The psalm opens with three names of God one after another ('El, 'Elohim, YHWH), as in Joshua 22:22, to present him in full majesty as the judge who calls the court to order.

decisions.choice: has spoken and summoned the earth: God calls a trial
decisions.reason: God summons the whole world as his court to hear a case against his own people (verse 4), as the prophets do (Isaiah 1:2; Micah 6:1-2).

decisions.choice: song
decisions.reason: As in 3:1.

records.heading: God brings his people to court

records.source: מִצִּיּ֥וֹן מִכְלַל־יֹ֗פִי אֱלֹהִ֥ים הוֹפִֽיעַ׃
records.gloss: From Zion, [the] perfection of beauty, God has shone forth.
pieces: God has blazed out from Zion, the city of flawless beauty.

L.2: From Zion, the perfection of beauty, God has shone forth.

R.2: God shines out like the sun from Zion, the most beautiful city.

decisions.choice: shone forth: God appears in light
decisions.reason: The verb (yafa') is used for God's appearing in brightness, as when he came from Sinai and "shone forth from Mount Paran" (Deuteronomy 33:2; compare 80:2).

decisions.choice: the perfection of beauty: Zion
decisions.reason: The phrase describes Zion, as in Lamentations 2:15. God now comes not from Sinai but from Zion, where he lives.

decisions.choice: like the sun
decisions.reason: Readable makes the picture of God's shining plain.

records.source: יָ֤בֹ֥א אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ וְֽאַל־יֶ֫חֱרַ֥שׁ אֵשׁ־לְפָנָ֥יו תֹּאכֵ֑ל וּ֝סְבִיבָ֗יו נִשְׂעֲרָ֥ה מְאֹֽד׃
records.gloss: Our God comes, and let him not keep silent; fire before him devours, and around him it storms exceedingly.
pieces: Our God is coming, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will not stay silent; a fire consumes all in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} path, and a fierce storm rages on every side.

L.3: Our God comes and does not keep silent; fire devours before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} it storms exceedingly.

R.3: Our God is coming, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will not be quiet. Fire burns up everything in front of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. A terrible storm blows all around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: fire and storm: as at Sinai
decisions.reason: Fire and storm came with God when he gave the covenant at Sinai (Exodus 19:16-18). He comes in the same way to call his people to account for it.

decisions.choice: does not keep silent: he will speak
decisions.reason: The form can be a statement or a wish. The silence that ends here is the one of verse 21, which the wicked mistook for approval.

records.source: יִקְרָ֣א אֶל־הַשָּׁמַ֣יִם מֵעָ֑ל וְאֶל־הָ֝אָ֗רֶץ לָדִ֥ין עַמּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: He summons the heavens from above and the earth, to judge his people:
pieces: He calls heaven above and earth below as witnesses, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} judges {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people:

L.4: He summons the heavens above, and the earth, to judge {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people:

R.4: He calls the sky and the earth to be witnesses while {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} judges {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people.

decisions.choice: heaven and earth: witnesses in court
decisions.reason: Heaven and earth were called as witnesses when the covenant was made (Deuteronomy 30:19; 32:1), and so they are called again when God brings his case.

decisions.choice: judge: hear the case of
decisions.reason: The verb (din) means to judge or plead a case. God judges his own people here, not the nations.

decisions.choice: as witnesses
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say why heaven and earth are called (m1).

records.source: אִסְפוּ־לִ֥י חֲסִידָ֑י כֹּרְתֵ֖י בְרִיתִ֣י עֲלֵי־זָֽבַח׃
records.gloss: Gather to me my faithful ones, those who cut my covenant over sacrifice.
pieces: "Bring together before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} loyal people, who sealed {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant with a sacrifice."

L.5: "Gather to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} faithful ones, those who cut {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant by sacrifice."

R.5: "Bring {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} faithful people to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. They made a covenant with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} by offering a sacrifice."

decisions.choice: Gather to me: God speaks
decisions.reason: God gives the order to his court, so the words are in quotation marks. The psalm does not say who is told to gather the people.

decisions.choice: cut my covenant by sacrifice: Sinai
decisions.reason: A covenant was "cut" with a sacrifice; at Sinai Moses sprinkled the blood of the offerings on the altar and on the people (Exodus 24:5-8).

decisions.choice: my faithful ones: my loyal people
decisions.reason: The word (chasidim) is the one of 4:4 and 12:2, here for all of Israel, the people bound to God by covenant, whether or not they live up to the name.

records.source: וַיַּגִּ֣ידוּ שָׁמַ֣יִם צִדְק֑וֹ כִּֽי־אֱלֹהִ֓ים׀שֹׁפֵ֖ט ה֣וּא סֶֽלָה׃
records.gloss: And the heavens declare his righteousness, for God, he [is] judging. Selah.
pieces: The heavens make known {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} justice, because it is God who sits as judge. Selah

L.6: And the heavens declare {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} righteousness, for God {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} [is] judge. Selah

R.6: The skies tell everyone that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is fair, because God {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} is the judge. Selah

decisions.choice: God himself is judge
alternatives: God is a God of justice
decisions.reason: The pronoun (hu') stresses that God himself sits in judgment; no lesser judge will hear this case.

decisions.choice: his righteousness: his justice as judge
decisions.reason: Righteousness (tsedeq) here is the fairness of the judge. The heavens, his witnesses, declare that his verdict will be just.

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
alternatives: lift up (the voice or the music)
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in Habakkuk 3. It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude; the ancient Greek translation renders it with a word meaning "interlude". It is not part of what is said, and here it marks a break after the line.

decisions.choice: Selah, kept as it is
decisions.reason: Its meaning is unknown (see the meaning decision on Selah), so every level keeps the word rather than guess, and keeps it apart from the sentence.

records.source: שִׁמְעָ֤ה עַמִּ֨י׀וַאֲדַבֵּ֗רָה יִ֭שְׂרָאֵל וְאָעִ֣ידָה בָּ֑ךְ אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֱלֹהֶ֣יךָ אָנֹֽכִי׃
records.gloss: Hear, my people, and I will speak; Israel, and I will testify against you; God, your God, [am] I.
pieces: "Pay attention, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, for I am about to speak; I am bringing testimony against you, Israel. I am God, your God.

L.7: "Hear, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, and I will speak; Israel, and I will testify against you: God, your God, [am] I.

R.7: "Listen, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people! I am going to speak. Israel, I am telling you what you have done wrong. I am God, your God.

decisions.choice: Hear, Israel ... I am God, your God
decisions.reason: The words echo the covenant: "Hear, Israel" (Deuteronomy 6:4) and "I am the LORD your God" at the head of the Ten Commandments (Exodus 20). Psalms 42-83 mostly say "God" where other psalms say "the LORD".

decisions.choice: testify against you: bring evidence as a witness
decisions.reason: The verb ('ud) means to bear witness or to warn solemnly. God is both judge and witness in this case.

decisions.choice: God's speech, to verse 15
decisions.reason: From here God speaks to his people to the end of verse 15; the quotation stays open until then.

records.source: לֹ֣א עַל־זְ֭בָחֶיךָ אוֹכִיחֶ֑ךָ וְעוֹלֹתֶ֖יךָ לְנֶגְדִּ֣י תָמִֽיד׃
records.gloss: Not on your sacrifices do I rebuke you, and your burnt offerings [are] before me continually.
pieces: I do not find fault with you over your sacrifices; your burnt offerings are always in front of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

L.8: Not for your sacrifices do I rebuke you, and your burnt offerings [are] before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} continually.

R.8: I am not angry at you because of your sacrifices. You always bring {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} burnt offerings.

decisions.choice: not for your sacrifices: the problem lies elsewhere
decisions.reason: God does not reject the sacrifices themselves; the people offer them faithfully. His complaint is about what they think sacrifice is (verses 9-13) and how they live (verses 16-21).

decisions.choice: burnt offerings, continually: the daily offering
decisions.reason: The burnt offering ('olah) was burned whole on the altar; one was offered every morning and evening (Exodus 29:38-42).

records.source: לֹא־אֶקַּ֣ח מִבֵּיתְךָ֣ פָ֑ר מִ֝מִּכְלְאֹתֶ֗יךָ עַתּוּדִֽים׃
records.gloss: Not I will take from your house a bull, from your folds goats.
pieces: I will not accept a young bull from your household, or male goats out of your sheepfolds.

L.9: I will not take a bull from your house, [or] goats from your folds.

R.9: I do not need to take a bull from your farm or goats from your flocks.

decisions.choice: I will not take: I have no need of them
decisions.reason: Verses 10-12 give the reason: God does not take the animals because he needs them; they are already his.

decisions.choice: bull, goats: animals for sacrifice
decisions.reason: The young bull (par) and the male goats ('attudim) were among the costliest offerings.

records.source: כִּי־לִ֥י כָל־חַיְתוֹ־יָ֑עַר בְּ֝הֵמ֗וֹת בְּהַרְרֵי־אָֽלֶף׃
records.gloss: For to me [belongs] every living thing of [the] forest, [the] animals on hills of a thousand.
pieces: For all the creatures of the woods belong to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and so do the herds grazing over a thousand hills.

L.10: For every living thing of [the] forest [is] {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}}, the cattle on a thousand hills.

R.10: All the wild animals in the forest belong to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. So do the cattle on thousands of hills.

decisions.choice: to me belongs: God owns all creatures
decisions.reason: Everything people could offer already belongs to God (24:1). A gift cannot make him richer.

decisions.choice: a thousand hills: countless hills
decisions.reason: A thousand stands for a great, uncounted number.

records.source: יָ֭דַעְתִּי כָּל־ע֣וֹף הָרִ֑ים וְזִ֥יז שָׂ֝דַ֗י עִמָּדִֽי׃
records.gloss: I know every bird of [the] mountains, and [the] moving creatures of [the] field [are] with me.
pieces: I know every bird of the high hills; whatever stirs in the open country is in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} keeping.

L.11: I know every bird of [the] mountains, and the moving creatures of [the] field [are] with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

R.11: I know every bird that lives on the mountains. All the creatures in the fields belong to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: moving creatures: the small creatures that swarm
decisions.reason: The word (ziz) is rare (80:14); it seems to mean whatever moves about in the fields, small animals or insects.

decisions.choice: I know: I know them as their owner
decisions.reason: To know them is to know each one as its owner and maker.

decisions.choice: with me: in my keeping, mine
decisions.reason: "With me" means they are present to him and under his care.

records.source: אִם־אֶ֭רְעַב לֹא־אֹ֣מַר לָ֑ךְ כִּי־לִ֥י תֵ֝בֵ֗ל וּמְלֹאָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: If I were hungry, not I would tell you, for to me [belongs the] world and its fullness.
pieces: Were I ever hungry, you are not the one I would tell, since the world and all it holds are {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}}.

L.12: If I were hungry, I would not tell you, for the world [is] {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}}, and all that fills it.

R.12: Even if I were hungry, I would not ask you for food. The whole world and everything in it is {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}}.

decisions.choice: the world and its fullness
decisions.reason: The same words open 24:1: "The earth is the LORD's and its fullness".

decisions.choice: If I were hungry: God needs no food
decisions.reason: Israel's neighbors set out food for their gods. God mocks the idea that his sacrifices feed him.

decisions.choice: ask you for food
decisions.reason: Readable says what telling would be for.

records.source: הַֽ֭אוֹכַל בְּשַׂ֣ר אַבִּירִ֑ים וְדַ֖ם עַתּוּדִ֣ים אֶשְׁתֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: Do I eat [the] flesh of mighty [bulls], and [the] blood of goats do I drink?
pieces: Am I one who eats the meat of bulls, or drinks the blood of goats?

L.13: Do I eat the flesh of mighty [bulls], or drink the blood of goats?

R.13: I do not feed on bulls' meat, and I do not drink goats' blood!

decisions.choice: mighty ones: bulls
decisions.reason: The word ('abbirim) means "mighty ones" and is used for strong bulls (22:13).

decisions.choice: a question that expects "no"
decisions.reason: The question mocks the idea that God feeds on sacrifices.

decisions.choice: a statement
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into what it means (m2).

records.source: זְבַ֣ח לֵאלֹהִ֣ים תּוֹדָ֑ה וְשַׁלֵּ֖ם לְעֶלְי֣וֹן נְדָרֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: Sacrifice to God thanksgiving, and pay to [the] Most High your vows,
pieces: Offer thanksgiving to God as your sacrifice, and keep the vows you made to the Most High,

L.14: Sacrifice a thank offering to God, and pay your vows to [the] Most High,

R.14: Instead, give thanks to God; let that be your sacrifice. Do what you promised the God who is above all.

decisions.choice: thanksgiving: a thank offering, or thanks itself
decisions.reason: The word (todah) is both the thank offering (Leviticus 7:12) and the thanks it expresses. What God wants is the grateful heart, given with or as the sacrifice (compare 51:18-19; Hebrews 13:15).

decisions.choice: pay your vows: do what you promised God
decisions.reason: A vow was a promise to God, often of an offering, made in time of need (Deuteronomy 23; 66:13-14).

decisions.choice: God speaks of himself as "God"
decisions.reason: God names himself in the third person, "God", "the Most High", as a king might in a royal decree; the speaker is still God.

decisions.choice: the God who is above all
decisions.reason: As in 46:5.

records.source: וּ֭קְרָאֵנִי בְּי֣וֹם צָרָ֑ה אֲ֝חַלֶּצְךָ֗ וּֽתְכַבְּדֵֽנִי׃
records.gloss: and call on me in [a] day of trouble; I will rescue you, and you will honor me.
pieces: and call to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} when trouble comes; I will set you free, and you will give {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} glory."

L.15: and call on {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in [the] day of trouble; I will rescue you, and you will honor {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

R.15: When you are in trouble, call to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} for help. I will save you, and you will praise {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

decisions.choice: call, rescue, honor: true worship
decisions.reason: What God wants from his people is trust that calls on him and thanks that honors him, not food (verses 12-13). His rescue leads to their praise.

decisions.choice: honor: give glory
decisions.reason: The verb (kabad, intensive) means to give weight and honor to someone; verse 23 uses it again.

records.source: וְלָ֤רָשָׁ֨ע׀אָ֘מַ֤ר אֱלֹהִ֗ים מַה־לְּ֭ךָ לְסַפֵּ֣ר חֻקָּ֑י וַתִּשָּׂ֖א בְרִיתִ֣י עֲלֵי־פִֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: But to the wicked God says, What [is it] to you to recount my statutes and [that] you have taken my covenant on your mouth?
pieces: But to the wicked God says: "What business do you have reciting {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} decrees, or mouthing the words of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant?

L.16: But to the wicked God says, "What [right is it] of yours to recount {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes, and [that] you have taken {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant on your mouth?

R.16: But God says to wicked people, "You have no right to repeat {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} laws or to talk about {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant!

decisions.choice: to the wicked: a second charge
decisions.reason: The first charge (verses 7-15) was about sacrifice; the second, to the end of the psalm, is about life. The wicked are members of the covenant people who recite God's law but break it.

decisions.choice: take my covenant on your mouth: speak of it, claim it
decisions.reason: They recite the covenant in worship and claim its promises, but do not keep it.

decisions.choice: the wicked (B); wicked people (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is singular, a type; the words that follow speak to each one as "you".

records.source: וְ֭אַתָּה שָׂנֵ֣אתָ מוּסָ֑ר וַתַּשְׁלֵ֖ךְ דְּבָרַ֣י אַחֲרֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: And you, you hate discipline, and you have cast my words behind you.
pieces: You hate to be corrected, and you toss {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words over your shoulder.

L.17: And you hate discipline, and you have cast {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words behind you.

R.17: You hate it when someone corrects you. You throw away what I tell you.

decisions.choice: discipline: correction, training
decisions.reason: The word (musar) is the correction a father gives a son, a key word of Proverbs (Proverbs 3:11-12).

decisions.choice: cast behind you: reject, ignore
decisions.reason: To throw something behind one's back is to refuse to look at it (Ezekiel 23:35).

records.source: אִם־רָאִ֣יתָ גַ֭נָּב וַתִּ֣רֶץ עִמּ֑וֹ וְעִ֖ם מְנָאֲפִ֣ים חֶלְקֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: If you saw a thief, you were pleased with him, and with adulterers [is] your portion.
pieces: You see a thief and are happy to go along with him; you share in what adulterers do.

L.18: When you saw a thief, you were pleased with him, and with adulterers [was] your portion.

R.18: When you see someone stealing, you go along with it. You spend your time with people who cheat on their husbands or wives.

decisions.choice: you were pleased with him
alternatives: you ran with him (the ancient Greek translation)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "you were pleased with him"; the ancient Greek translation, reading a similar word, has "you ran with him". The sense is close.

decisions.choice: thief, adulterers: the commandments broken
decisions.reason: Verses 18-20 name sins against the commandments not to steal, not to commit adultery and not to bear false witness (Exodus 20). Those who recite the covenant break it.

decisions.choice: your portion: your share, your company
decisions.reason: To have one's portion with someone is to join in what they do.

records.source: פִּ֭יךָ שָׁלַ֣חְתָּ בְרָעָ֑ה וּ֝לְשׁוֹנְךָ֗ תַּצְמִ֥יד מִרְמָֽה׃
records.gloss: Your mouth you have let loose for evil, and your tongue harnesses deceit.
pieces: You let your mouth run free to do harm, and your tongue weaves lies.

L.19: Your mouth you have let loose for evil, and your tongue harnesses deceit.

R.19: You say evil things whenever you like, and you use your tongue to lie.

decisions.choice: harnesses: yokes, binds together
decisions.reason: The verb (tsamad) means to yoke or fasten (Numbers 25:3): their tongue is harnessed to deceit, or fits lies together.

decisions.choice: let loose your mouth: speak without restraint
decisions.reason: The mouth is sent out freely, like an animal let off its rope.

records.gloss: You sit, against your brother you speak; against [the] son of your mother you give a blemish.
pieces: You sit around speaking against your brother; you smear the name of your own mother's son.

L.20: You sit [and] speak against your brother; against your own mother's son you give slander.

R.20: You sit and talk against your own brother. You tell lies about your mother's son.

decisions.choice: a blemish: a fault, slander
decisions.reason: The word (dofi) occurs only here; it means a fault or stain, and so a damaging word against someone.

decisions.choice: you sit: you sit together, perhaps in council
decisions.reason: Sitting may picture idle talk among friends, or sitting in the town gate where cases were heard, where false witness could ruin a brother.

decisions.choice: your mother's son: your own brother
decisions.reason: The phrase stresses the closest family tie.

records.source: אֵ֤לֶּה עָשִׂ֨יתָ׀וְֽהֶחֱרַ֗שְׁתִּי דִּמִּ֗יתָ הֱֽיוֹת־אֶֽהְיֶ֥ה כָמ֑וֹךָ אוֹכִיחֲךָ֖ וְאֶֽעֶרְכָ֣ה לְעֵינֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: These you have done, and I kept silent; you thought that I was surely like you; I will rebuke you and set [it] in order before your eyes.
pieces: You did these things and I said nothing, so you imagined I was no different from you. Now I will rebuke you and lay out the case before your eyes.

L.21: These [things] you have done, and I kept silent; you thought that I was altogether like you. I will rebuke you and set [it] in order before your eyes.

R.21: You did all these things, and I did not say anything. So you thought I was like you. But now I will correct you. I will show you clearly everything you have done wrong.

decisions.choice: I kept silent: patience, not approval
decisions.reason: God's silence was patience, but they took it as agreement. Now he "does not keep silent" (verse 3).

decisions.choice: that I was surely like you
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for stress: they thought God was just like them, that he approved of what they approved.

decisions.choice: set it in order before your eyes: lay out the charges
decisions.reason: The verb ('arak) is used of drawing up a legal case (Job 23:4). God sets out the evidence in front of them.

records.source: בִּֽינוּ־נָ֣א זֹ֭את שֹׁכְחֵ֣י אֱל֑וֹהַּ פֶּן־אֶ֝טְרֹ֗ף וְאֵ֣ין מַצִּֽיל׃
records.gloss: Understand this, please, [you who] forget God, lest I tear [you] and there be no rescuer.
pieces: Now take this to heart, all of you who forget God, or I will tear you apart like a lion, and no one will be able to save you.

L.22: Understand this now, [you who] forget God, lest I tear [you] apart and there be none to rescue.

R.22: You people who forget God, think about this! If you do not, I will tear you apart, and no one will be able to save you.

decisions.choice: tear: as a lion tears its prey
decisions.reason: The verb (taraf) is used of lions tearing prey (7:3; Hosea 5). The God who rescues (verse 15) will be the one from whom no one can rescue.

decisions.choice: forget God: live as though he did not matter
decisions.reason: To forget God is not a lapse of memory but a life that ignores him (Deuteronomy 8:11-14).

decisions.choice: like a lion
decisions.reason: Balanced makes the picture in the verb plain (m1).

records.source: זֹבֵ֥חַ תּוֹדָ֗ה יְֽכַ֫בְּדָ֥נְנִי וְשָׂ֥ם דֶּ֑רֶךְ אַ֝רְאֶ֗נּוּ בְּיֵ֣שַׁע אֱלֹהִֽים׃
records.gloss: [One who] sacrifices thanksgiving honors me, and [one who] sets [the] way, I will let him see the salvation of God.
pieces: Whoever offers thanks as a sacrifice gives {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} honor, and whoever walks the right road, I will let them see how God saves."

L.23: Whoever sacrifices thanksgiving honors {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and to {{gender:the one|him}} who sets [the] way I will show the salvation of God."

R.23: People who thank {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} as their offering are honoring {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. If you live the right way, I will show you how God saves."

decisions.choice: sets the way: keeps to the right road
alternatives: the one whose way is blameless (with a small change)
decisions.reason: The phrase is hard: literally "who sets a way". It may mean one who orders their life rightly, or one who prepares a way for God to show his salvation. With a small change it would read "the one whose way is blameless".

decisions.choice: thanksgiving honors me: the two charges answered
decisions.reason: The psalm ends by joining its two charges: true sacrifice is thanks (verse 14), and the right way of life (verses 16-21) leads to God's salvation.

decisions.choice: the salvation of God: God's rescue
decisions.reason: Salvation (yesha') is God's saving help, as in 12:6.

decisions.choice: the one, with "him" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The phrase means anyone who lives this way.
